entries.title: Target identity is content-addressed
entries.statement: Claims and evidence are bound to an exact target digest; a title or version label is not a substitute for content identity.
consequences: Reject evidence whose target digest differs from the active target identity.
limitations: Digest equality proves identity, not provenance, legality, or canonicality.

entries.title: Observed boundaries require independent coverage
entries.statement: A disassembler-created function extent is an observation and cannot become an accepted complete boundary without sufficient independent coverage.
consequences: Return incomplete when an observed extent covers less than the accepted extent.
limitations: The first counterexample is segmented PC-98 code; it does not quantify error rates for other analysis tools or platforms.

entries.title: Relocation edges and destination contents are distinct evidence
entries.statement: Matching relocation type, addend, and destination address does not prove equality of the bytes stored at the destination.
consequences: Attest referenced literal or data bytes before accepting a relocation-dependent exact claim.
limitations: The fixture covers a VC7 DIR32 floating literal; providers must define encoding rules for other relocation and data kinds.

entries.title: Function exactness does not imply product closure
entries.statement: Source presence, exact function replay, translation-unit compilation, link closure, whole-image equality, and runtime validation are separate claims.
consequences: Never derive whole_build_closed from function, byte, source, or object progress metrics.
limitations: The fixture disproves one implication; it does not prescribe a universal linker or runtime oracle.

entries.title: Physical ownership does not imply exactness
entries.statement: Owned source-function bytes may include exclusions and noncontiguous chunks, while exactness for each covered lane remains independently unproved.
consequences: Compute physical byte ownership from an extent graph and grant exact credit only to independently verified extents.
limitations: The initial evidence covers two VC8 LTCG giant roots and must not be used to infer noncontiguous ownership for every function.

entries.title: Source-name cardinality is not function cardinality
entries.statement: A source-level implementation name may map to more than one target function identity, so progress must count the intended identity domain.
consequences: Count source-present functions over target identities rather than unique implementation strings.
limitations: The fixture establishes one TH08 authored alias group; other repositories may use one-to-one or different mapping rules.

entries.title: Toolchain identity is a surface set
entries.statement: An exact toolchain and oracle-environment identity includes every pinned compiler, assembler, linker, configuration, header, library, startup, and execution surface required by its provider.
consequences: Return incomplete when any provider-required toolchain surface is absent from the identity fingerprint.
limitations: The fourteen concrete surfaces belong to the reviewed TH04 profile; another provider may require a different set.

entries.title: Codegen context explains but does not waive byte mismatch
entries.statement: Standalone and linked whole-program codegen contexts may produce different physical layouts, but observed differing bytes still reject an exact claim.
consequences: Keep the claim non-exact while context recovery remains an open cause of observed byte differences.
limitations: Different codegen context alone is not a failure when complete comparison independently proves equal target bytes.

entries.title: Exact evidence is claim-scoped
entries.statement: A passing oracle result is reusable only when its artifact, unit, target extent, and other required identity fields match the exact claim being evaluated.
consequences: Reject passing evidence rebound to another unit or extent, even when every oracle ID and result value is otherwise valid.
limitations: Global and artifact-scoped oracle classes remain valid only when explicitly declared by the provider policy.

entries.title: Concurrent mutable tools require invocation-scoped workspaces
entries.statement: Concurrent invocations of a tool that writes intermediates must not share the same case-insensitive workspace identity.
consequences: Allocate unique provider-valid workspace paths before concurrent compiler, assembler, linker, or attestation probes run.
limitations: The concrete eight-character naming rule is required by the reviewed DOS profile, not by every modern toolchain.

entries.title: Cross-platform runtime equivalence
entries.statement: A common acceptance contract for replay-driven runtime equivalence across PC-98 emulators, Windows, Wine, and native ports has not yet been established in the factory.
limitations: Existing repositories contain platform-specific smoke and runtime work, but no reviewed shared receipt schema has been imported here.

entries.title: VC8 linked LTCG reproduction
entries.statement: A general recipe for reproducing every shipped VC8 LTCG physical-owner merge and placement decision is not known.
limitations: Many individual functions are exact under focused reconstruction; this unknown applies only where linked layout context remains necessary.
